about.heading: About Me
paragraphs: I'm Sukesh Surase — a full-stack developer and designer who builds across the entire stack. From crafting pixel-perfect UIs and smooth animations to architecting APIs, databases, and CRM systems, I'm comfortable wherever the work takes me.

My work spans full-stack web development, business systems, XR / VR experiences, UI/UX design, creative media production, copywriting, and public speaking & event hosting. That mix lets me move fluidly between the technical and the creative — shaping both how a product works and how it makes people feel.

I'm driven by craft and curiosity. Whether it's an immersive VR campus tour on Meta Quest 3, a full-featured CRM platform, or a polished travel-guide web app, I aim to ship experiences that are bold, accessible, and genuinely useful.

projects.title: VR Campus Tour
projects.description: An interactive virtual reality campus tour that lets prospective students explore facilities in immersive 3D.
projects.longDescription: A fully immersive XR campus tour built in Unity, scripted in C#, and deployed on Meta Quest 3. Real-world spaces were captured using Polycam for 3D scanning and Insta360 for 360° photography, then assembled into an interactive walkthrough with spatial navigation and hotspots.

projects.title: KL The Guide Web
projects.description: A polished travel-guide web platform helping visitors discover the best of Kuala Lumpur.
projects.longDescription: A content-rich travel guide with curated destinations, dynamic filtering, and a responsive editorial layout. Built with JavaScript on the front-end, SQL powering the database layer, and Figma driving the visual design — focused on fast load times, intuitive navigation, and a vibrant identity that captures the energy of the city.

projects.title: SJSS Web
projects.description: A modern business website and system built end-to-end for clarity, speed, and a strong brand presence.
projects.longDescription: A full-stack build for the SJSS platform covering a polished marketing website and internal system UI. Emphasises a clean component architecture, accessible forms, and a cohesive design system — built to scale with reusable UI patterns and a smooth, professional user experience.

projects.title: SJRenovation CRM
projects.description: A full-featured CRM system for a renovation company — managing customers, quotations, and project pipelines.
projects.longDescription: An end-to-end CRM platform built for SJ Renovation, featuring customer management, quotation generation, project tracking, and file uploads. Designed with a clean dashboard UI and a RESTful API backend for streamlined day-to-day business operations. Currently in active development.

projects.title: Bella Cucina Ordering System
projects.description: A complete restaurant ordering and CRM platform — customer storefront, kitchen display and POS, and an admin back office, all on one database.
projects.longDescription:
A client-ready online ordering system for F&B businesses, built as three surfaces over a single schema. Customers browse a modifier-aware menu, run a five-step checkout, track their order live and earn loyalty points. Staff work a kitchen ticket queue with SLA timers, build walk-in orders, split bills and manage a table floor plan. Owners get analytics, menu management, a rules-enforcing voucher engine, and CRM segmentation with campaign recipes.

The architecture is deliberately server-authoritative: all pricing — subtotals, voucher validation, promotion stacking, tier discounts, fees, tax and points — lives in one server-only module, and the client re-quotes on every change rather than ever computing a price. Roles are enforced server-side, not merely hidden in the UI, and the loyalty points ledger is append-only with derived balances, so refunds claw points back automatically. It runs on a local SQLite file with simulated payments out of the box, and swaps to Turso and Stripe for production without a dialect change.

projects.title: YLDI.ManUtd
projects.description: A mobile-first progressive web app for calling Manchester United scorelines against your friends — private leagues, deadline-enforced predictions and a season-long leaderboard.
projects.longDescription:
A football prediction PWA built around private leagues: create one, share an invite code, and call the scoreline before kickoff. Alongside straight predictions it runs a token betting layer — scoreline, multi-scorer and knockout bets, with a parlay bonus — settled idempotently so a replayed result can never double-pay. The app also carries fixtures and matchday pages with a live event timeline, the Premier League table, a squad list with position filtering, player profiles and a trophy cabinet, plus an admin dashboard for scorers, squad stats, leagues and data syncs.

Scoring and the leaderboard are deterministic and idempotent by design, so the same inputs always settle to the same standings. It ships as an installable PWA with a service worker and offline page, runs entirely on free tiers, and develops against a mock data provider so the whole app works with no API key at all.

projects.title: Morgana AI
projects.description: A voice-first, JARVIS-style AI assistant that remembers me across sessions, acts through its own tools and reaches out proactively — now being rebuilt as a licensed, multi-tenant product.
projects.longDescription:
Morgana began as my own voice-first assistant in Python: a streaming conversation core, a pluggable tool registry, speech in and out, long-term memory, and an always-on proactive loop. Beyond answering, she acts — managing tasks and reminders, searching my notes, reporting system status, and running a background heartbeat that surfaces things quietly and only interrupts when it matters. Every consequential action passes through a hard per-action confirmation gate with a full audit log and a one-command kill switch.

Version two turns that personal build into something sellable. The single-tenant core is being split into a local agent plus a thin cloud: a model gateway that meters token usage without ever logging prompt bodies, and a real licensing service that issues, activates, device-binds, verifies and revokes Ed25519-signed licences with an offline grace period. A desktop dashboard with an original animated HUD avatar drives it from the tray. The demo build runs with no model key at all — a scripted provider sits behind the same seam as the live one — so sign-up and payment are simulated while the cryptography, device binding and quota enforcement are the real, tested code paths.
